newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Centaur says has major gold find.
newsitem.headline: Centaur says has major gold find.

text.p: Centaur Mining and Exploration Ltd on Wednesday said it had made a major gold discovery at its Woodcutters tenements, about 40 km north of Kalgoorlie in Western Australia.
The company also lifted the resource estimate at its Mt Pleasant and Ora Banda desposits in Western Australia by 1.8 million ounces to 5.7 million ounces.
"Drilling is continuing to outline additional resources and delineation of reserves," Centaur said in its quarterly report.

"Independent consulting engineers have been appointed to accelerate the mineral resource and proven and probable reserve estimates at Mt Pleasant, Ora Banda and those anticipated at Woodcutters by the end of June 1997," it said.

Centaur said the Woodcutters discovery, to be known as Federal, achieved best results of 28 metres at 9.1 grams per tonne of gold from 76 metres, 20 metres at 7.6 g/t from 104 metres and 16 metres at 13.3 g/t from 34 metres.
"This gold discovery highlights the prospectivity of the granite rock east of the Boulder-Lefroy fault over which the company holds tenements covering a length of 50 km," it said.
Centaur produced 42,476 ounces of gold for the quarter at a cash operating cost of A$457 per ounce.
Production during April would total about 15,000 ounces at a cash operating cost of about A$360 an ounce, it said.
Centaur shares closed 11 cents firmer at A$1.70, with more than eight million shares changing hands.
